comparator.name: Chemical Engineering
comparator.sourceNotes: The current 2026–2027 Ocasys programme and official bachelor page identify a 180-EC Chemical Engineering bachelor. The formal appendix supplies the complete component structure: a compulsory 60-EC first year, 105 EC of compulsory upper-year courses and 15 EC of approved electives. The official 2026–2027 PDF URL and TER landing label the appendix for 2026–2027, although its repeated page header still says 2025/2026; the current Ocasys curriculum and current programme page corroborate the listed structure and course set. The 15-EC approved-elective space is retained as restricted choice rather than populated with arbitrary selections. The ordinary single bachelor has no named route to select.

alternatives.label: Biochemistry, sustainable production & resource systems
alternatives.concept: Combine biomolecular and laboratory science with environmental biogeochemistry, lifecycle analysis, resource recovery, renewable systems, mathematics, programming, data and product design. This is a related-fields response to sustainable chemical-production interests, not Chemical Engineering equivalence.
alternatives.labelReason: The completed curriculum combines biochemistry and molecular laboratory work with lifecycle analysis, environmental biogeochemistry, resource recovery, renewable systems and quantitative product-design methods; the label does not claim chemistry or process-engineering formation.
progression: All 24 courses are unique, four occur in each fixed semester, Personal & Professional Development is in Year 1 and eight courses are level 300. Every formal prerequisite occurs earlier and every course is available in its assigned term. Life-science foundations precede molecular biology, biochemistry, laboratory work and molecular pathology; Sustainability Essentials I precedes II and dependent advanced resource courses; Mathematical Methods precedes numerical methods and probability.

candidates.label: Chemical reactors, transport, thermodynamics and process-plant design

selection.assessment: One complete related-fields programme passes the evidence, relevance and mechanical gates. It responds to sustainable production, molecular innovation, lower-impact materials, carbon management, renewable systems and industrial cost/efficiency through actual biochemistry, environmental science, lifecycle, resource, energy, quantitative and design content. It is explicitly not presented as Chemical Engineering. A second process-engineering direction cannot supply cumulative chemistry, thermodynamics, transport phenomena, reactors, separations, process control, process equipment, chemical-engineering practicals or process design; padding it with adjacent science and sustainability courses would not create a defensible curriculum.

blocks: Biochemistry, cells and molecular laboratory work
Both introduce molecular foundations; UCR centres biomolecules, cells and DNA, while the external component establishes chemical structure and reactivity.
Both address biochemical mechanisms and biotechnology; UCR studies biomolecules and metabolism rather than engineering biochemical production.
Both establish calculus and mathematical tools for later scientific work; UCR is general rather than chemistry- and engineering-specific.
Both develop numerical solution methods; UCR provides general computational mathematics rather than chemical-engineering applications.
Environmental chemistry, lifecycle, energy and resources
Both establish sustainability questions using science and project work; UCR provides an interdisciplinary sustainability foundation rather than chemical-process engineering.
Both examine how production choices affect environmental outcomes; UCR focuses lifecycle and circular-economy analysis and does not teach green-chemistry reactions.
Both address product development and evaluation; UCR teaches general consumer-product design rather than chemical product formulation and industrial production.

notes.text: The UCR programme combines biochemistry and molecular laboratory work with environmental biogeochemistry, lifecycle analysis, resource recovery, renewable systems and quantitative product-design methods. It does not reproduce the target’s organic, inorganic and physical chemistry; spectroscopy and synthesis; thermodynamics and transport phenomena; reactors, separations, process control and equipment; polymer engineering; chemical-engineering practicals, process design or discipline-specific research project.
